## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3f5a08241e34e7659e594dc32382ce32fd3e881a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: none (reviewFace returns no hits; the PR is ungoverned) + scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs, scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs, scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs

PR #33687, card #33541. Read: the card body and its four comments (triage 6886847470, added scope 6887864752, claim 6890056280, os-dev-report 6890395401), the PR body, the three-file net diff against `main` (merge base `d4e3dcc6`), and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read in the head tree only to judge the three files: `locateReviewOfRecord`, `regenCarry`, `latestMarkedComment`, `recordVerdict`, `makeCommentReader`, `FLEET_BOT_LOGIN`, `GOVERNED_APPROVERS`, `governed-surface-guard.yml`, `fleet-write.yml`.

### ① Derived judgments

- Tier S record leg, accept set NARROWS: a record that stands now clears only with exactly one explicit verdict line under its heading and that line reading PASS. FAIL, zero lines, two lines each become `not-pass` (exit 3) naming the comment id. Right: this is card item 1 and AGENTS.md Prime Directive 14 ("a PASS verdict").
- Low-risk skills arm, accept set NARROWS: it read `contractReviewVerdictOf` (explicit, then heading-inline, then bare); it now reads the counting form, so a record whose only verdict is heading-inline or bare is refused. Right: the seat's ruling is one rule on every leg; the template has printed the explicit line since #18042.
- Author binding, accept set NARROWS: rows whose `user.login` is not `FLEET_BOT_LOGIN` or in `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` are dropped in `runGuard` before `recordVerdict`, so before the locator and before `regenProvenanceHops`. Right against the seat's ruling (narrower than comment 6887864752's "organisation member", on the seat's word). The same filter covers the carry chain, since `regenCarry` reads the same `pair` rows.
- One effect in the other direction, by design: an untrusted row no longer SHADOWS. A newer same-head FAIL, unsigned or below-tier record by an untrusted author used to be the locator's newest and refuse; it is now unread and an older trusted PASS clears. Right under the ruling ("ignored"), and pinned (`shadowFail`), but see nit N1.
- Loader: `verdictOf` is replaced by `verdictLines`, now REQUIRED, and `trustedAuthors` is required. A missing reader or an empty or non-string `FLEET_BOT_LOGIN` makes the whole set `available: false`, which `recordVerdict` turns into `unreadable`. Fail-closed, right. A set injected without `trustedAuthors` trusts nobody (`recordAuthorTrusted` needs an array), right.
- `record-recognisers.mjs` export surface: `contractReviewVerdictOf` re-export removed, `contractReviewVerdictLines` added. No other importer of the removed re-export exists in the head tree (grep). Right.
- `RECOGNISER_SOURCES` gains `author`; the source pin moves from one key to two. Right.
- No package, schema or published surface changes.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right: all three paths are `scripts/pm/**`, published by no package; the `Check Changeset` run on this head concluded success.
Clause-②: no. Agreed: nothing in `packages/spec`, no protocol or public API surface.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation, file surface widened to `check-half-states.mjs`: covered by the seat's ruling (one reader, a sibling export on the same regex). The diff there is the export, one docblock and one H43 row. Accepted.
- Deviation, PR-body signature as a prose line and a model-free `Co-Authored-By`: not contract matters; the trailer gate is one of the runs still in progress (below). Left to the seat.
- Acceptance note, register reads `scripts/pm/**` as NOT governed while the card says Tier S: `reviewFace` returns no hits, so the landing route is the ordinary queue; the Tier S wording on the card is the seat's per-card review call, not a register fact. Answered, no escalation.
- Out-of-scope finding, `check-owed-reviews.mjs` spells its own `VERDICT_LINE`: confirmed display only (`verdictOf` feeds a column). See follow-up F1.
- Check-runs on this head. Concluded success: Governed Surface Queue Guard (its job runs the guard's `--self-test`, live loader included, under the sparse checkout), PR-body guards, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Type Check · workspace, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Plan Test Core shards, Live required-set sweep, Platform checklist gate sweep, Release section-coverage sweep, filter, Auto Label. STILL IN PROGRESS when read: Lint · CI, release and engine gates; Lint · ESLint; Lint · PM dispatch-gates; Lint · docs and code guards; Lint · repo and tooling gates; Lint · scoped · slot lookup and corpus; Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests; Live half-state sweep; Test Core (1/8); Test Core (2/8); Type Check · consumer gates; Type Check · debt ledger; Type Check · source gates. The `record-recognisers` and `check-half-states` self-tests ride the pending Lint jobs, so this record does not vouch for them; landing waits on them going green. No failure on the head when read.

### ④ Design judgment

Contract: card #33541 items 1 to 3, comment 6887864752 (item D), and the seat's ruling (one reader; exactly one verdict line reading PASS on the newest same-head record; FAIL, none, two refuse; authors are the relay plus `GOVERNED_APPROVERS`, carry chain included).

Holds, with the attempts made to break it:

- Newest FAIL over an older PASS: `locateReviewOfRecord` picks the newest on-head row across both threads by `created_at` (thread order on a tie or an unreadable stamp), and `recordPassVerdict` reads that row by id. Refused. The reverse clears. Both pinned.
- Carried record: the carry is consulted only when no same-head record exists, and the old-head read must return the id the chain names, so a newer FAIL on the old head breaks the carry (id mismatch, absent). The verdict is read off the carried comment itself.
- Quoted or fenced verdict line: the explicit regex admits a leading blockquote mark and has no fence awareness, so such a line COUNTS and the record is refused as two lines. Fail-closed, as ruled.
- Inline and bare dialects: zero explicit lines, refused. An inline PASS beside one explicit line is not a second line.
- Edited comments: the REST row keeps the original `user`; editing another account's comment needs write access, and a write-access holder can already post through the relay (`fleet-write.yml` gates on the sender's permission on the target). No wider than the trusted set.
- Quoted record inside a trusted comment: the head reader needs a real heading (at most three spaces of indent), so a blockquoted record names no head and is no record. The verdict count starts at the FIRST heading marker, which sits at or above the heading the head was read from, so it can only over-count.
- Untrusted carry hop: dropped with the row, carries nothing. Pinned.
- Loader failing or empty: unavailable, never trust-everyone. Pinned. The live import graph loads in the guard's own CI job.
- Production rows: `makeCommentReader` returns the raw REST rows, so `user.login` is present; the binding cannot refuse everything by reading a projected row.
- Both legs: `runGuard` routes the arm through `lowRiskRecordVerdict`, which ends in `recordPassVerdict`, and every other Tier S entry straight to it. Only `stands` clears (`entrySatisfied`).

Docblocks read against the code, sentence by sentence: the guard header, `recordAuthorTrusted`, `recordPassVerdict`, `lowRiskRecordVerdict`, the `RECOGNISER_SOURCES` note, the `locateReviewOfRecord` note and the patrol reader's note all agree with the tree. No stale "existence and provenance" wording remains.

Findings: no must-fix, no should-fix.

- N1 (nit, prose face): the PR body's "only refuses more, never passes more" is not exact. An untrusted newer FAIL (for example one a seat posts from its own account by mistake) used to refuse on the arm and is now unread, so an older relay PASS clears, and the clearing words do not mention the ignored comment (the information line prints on an absent record only). This is the ruled behaviour; fix the sentence in the PR body, and take "print the ignored-author line on a clear too" as a follow-up card.
- N2 (nit, follow-up card): a self-contradicting record clears. A heading that reads FAIL above an explicit PASS line left from the template, or a FAIL spelled in a form the regex does not match (lower-case key, list bullet) beside one matching PASS line, counts as one PASS line. Same answer as `contractReviewVerdictOf` and exactly the ruled condition, so not a defect of this diff; a later card can refuse when the heading tail states the other word.
- N3 (nit, follow-up card): explicit lines ABOVE the heading are not counted (the reader starts under the first marker). Template records put the heading first.
- N4 (nit, accepted deviation): comment 6887864752 says an unreadable author "refuses"; the code ignores the row. A record with no readable author still clears nothing, which is the substance; a newer unreadable-author FAIL does not shadow, same as N1.
- N5 (nit, accepted): when only `trustedAuthors` is missing, the loader's reason still says the recognisers "live in ./record-recognisers.mjs, and a rename is the likely cause"; the bracketed item names `check-handover.mjs` correctly. The battery row titled "exit 4" asserts `available === false` and the reason, not the exit code.
- F1 (follow-up, outside the diff, read not reviewed): `check-owed-reviews.mjs` and the H43 patrol (`latestContractReviewOnHead`) read no author and take the first verdict match, so a patrol can show a review as current or PASS where the guard now refuses. Display and patrol only; worth one card so the three readings agree.
